sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Today's video is packed with 31 trending self-hosted projects from developer tools to media servers and productivity platforms you can run entirely on your own hardware. Let's go.

sections.title: Lidify
paragraphs: Litify. It's the missing link that connects your Spotify discovery directly to your LAR server. Instead of manually adding artists every time you find a new banger, this bot watches your liked songs and playlists in real time. You hard a track on your phone and it automatically forces LAR to monitor the artist and grab the album for your home server. It runs in Docker and finally lets you use streaming algorithms to build a collection you actually own.

sections.title: XPipe
paragraphs: Xpipe is the versatile connection hub that bridges your local desktop with your entire server fleet. It requires zero installation on the remote side. It just piggybacks off your existing SSH, Docker, or Kubernetes setups. You can browse remote files using your local explorer, open them directly in VS Code, and even drag and drop data between different servers. It runs locally, keeps your keys secure.

sections.title: Anchor
paragraphs: Ankor, the self-hosted Google Keep alternative that respects your privacy. You get the familiar card-based UI, rich markdown support, and a proper mobile PWA that feels native on your phone. The best part, it works completely offline and syncs up the second you reconnect. It spins up with a single Docker command and finally gives you a digital notebook that is 100% yours and 0% ad supported.

sections.title: omni-tools
paragraphs: Omni Tools, the self-hosted Swiss Army knife that replaces all those sketchy utility sites. It packs over 80 privacy first tools into a single dashboard that you run on your own server. You get everything from PDF mergers and image compressors to video trimmers and AI background removers. The best part, it runs 100% locally in your browser. No ads, no tracking, and your data never leaves your network.

sections.title: solidtime
paragraphs: Solid time is the open- source alternative to Toggle and Harvest that feels good to use. It gives you a slick, responsive interface to manage clients, set billable rates, and visualize exactly where your day went. You can generate detailed reports for invoices and manage multiple organizations without hitting a payw wall. It deploys instantly with Docker and finally lets you clock in without clocking up a massive SAS bill.

sections.title: Dozzle
paragraphs: This is Dazzle and it is the real-time log viewer for your Docker containers. It is lightweight. No database, no complex setup. You just run it and it gives you a beautiful web interface for all your logs. You can fuzzy search for errors, watch CPU and memory stats in real time. And my favorite part, split screen. You can debug your database and your API side by side without leaving the browser. If you have a home lab or a VPS, this is a mandatory install.

sections.title: Wallos
paragraphs: Wallace, the open-source personal finance tool designed to stop the bleeding. It's a self-hosted dashboard that tracks every single recurring payment from Netflix to that random gym membership. It visualizes your monthly burn rate, supports multiple currencies, and most importantly, sends you an alert before the payment hits, giving you the chance to cancel the service before you get charged again.

sections.title: Dawarich
paragraphs: Dwarich, the self-hosted alternative to Google Maps timeline that puts you in control of your location history. With Google locking down timeline data to mobile devices, Darich lets you build your own private travel archive. It imports your old Google takeout files and syncs live with apps like Overland to map every step you take. It generates beautiful heat maps, tracks your travel statistics like countries visited and miles traveled, and visualizes your life on a global scale.

sections.title: Linkwarden
paragraphs: Link Warden, the self-hosted bookmark manager that ensures you never lose a web page again. We've all clicked a bookmark only to find a 404 error because the site died. Link fixes this by acting as your own private wayback machine. The moment you save a URL, it captures a screenshot and a PDF of the page, archiving it forever on your server, ensuring that even if the internet changes, your data stays exactly the way you found it. Run Tippy, the operating system that makes self-hosting accessible to everyone.

sections.title: Runtipi
paragraphs: If you want to run your own personal cloud, but are intimidated by Docker containers and Linux command lines, TP is the answer. It turns your Raspberry Pi or old computer into a plug-and-play server with a beautiful dashboard. It features a one-click app store that lets you install NexCloud, Plex, or Adguard Home instantly, handling all the complex port mapping and configuration in the background.

sections.title: Mini QR
paragraphs: We've all been there. You make a QR code, print it out, and a week later it stops working because the site wants a monthly subscription. Mini QR fixes this. It's a dead simple privacy first tool that runs entirely in your browser. It generates static, permanent codes that never expire with no ads, no tracking, and no data leaving your device. It lets you customize colors, download SVGs, and finally share links without worrying about them breaking behind a payw wall.

sections.title: GoBackup
paragraphs: If you're still writing 200line bash scripts to dump your Postgress database, zip it up and upload it to S3, you are doing it wrong. Go backup lets you define your entire backup strategy in one simple YAML file. It natively supports every major database from MySQL to MongoDB and automatically compresses and ships your data to cloud storage like AWS or Google Cloud. It even handles pruning old files automatically, giving you a recovery plan that works.

sections.title: OCRBase
paragraphs: OCRBS, the self-hosted engine that turns your messy PDFs into usable JSON. It wraps powerful tools like Paddle OCR and local LLMs into a slick API that extracts structured data from documents with accuracy. You just spin up the Docker container and start blasting images at it. It's perfect for processing invoices, scanning receipts, or digitizing archives while keeping your data private and your costs at zero.

sections.title: Your LastFM
paragraphs: Your last FM, the minimal dashboard that respects your listening history. It syncs every single scrabble into a local lightning fast database so you can analyze your top tracks, albums, and obsessions instantly. No ads, no lag, just a clean mobile first interface that runs entirely on your own hardware. It spins up with Docker Compose and finally gives you a dedicated private home for your music data that's always online, even when the main site isn't.

sections.title: SafeLine
paragraphs: If you host a website, you know you need a firewall, but standard WFTs rely on regular expressions, which are messy, slow, and constantly block real users by mistake. Safeeline changes the game. It ditches the rejects for intelligent semantic analysis. It can tell the difference between a real SQL injection and just a weird looking URL. It installs with one Docker command, has a beautiful dashboard.

sections.title: Open Pace
paragraphs: This is open pace. Instead of uploading your GPS files to a corporate server that effectively owns them, this lets you host everything yourself. But here is the cool part. It uses Activity Pub. That means you can post a run and your friend on a totally different server or even on Mastadon can see it, like it, and comment. It's decentralized. It's open source. You actually own your workout history.

sections.title: blocky
paragraphs: If you love Pi Hole but hate clicking through web interfaces to manage it, you need to check out Blocky. It's a DNS ad blocker written in Go, which means it's ridiculously fast and lightweight. You configure the whole thing in one simple YAML file, perfect for GitOps or anyone who wants to version control their network config. The grouping feature is genius, too. You can strictly block Tik Tok on your kid's iPad while keeping it open on your phone, all from the same server.

sections.title: secrux
paragraphs: I honestly hate running security audits because it's usually just hours of scrolling through false positives. But I found this CLI tool called Crrux that actually uses AI to understand your code context. You point it at your repo and instead of just dumping a generic error log, it analyzes the logic to find real vulnerabilities like SQL injections or hard-coded keys.

sections.title: trip
paragraphs: Let's be real. Your dream vacation is currently rotting in a chaotic Google Maps list or a spreadsheet nobody reads. You need to spin up Trip. It's a self-hosted travel hub that takes all those random pins and turns them into an actual itinerary. You can map out points of interest, drag and drop your schedule, and collaborate with friends, all without some creepy app tracking your location data. It imports your existing maps, runs in Docker.

sections.title: Your Spotify
paragraphs: Waiting 365 days for Spotify wrapped to tell you that you listen to death. Taylor Swift is actual torture. You need to self-host your Spotify. It's basically a personal data warehouse for your music habits that runs right on your own server. It records every single stream in real time, giving you those deep dive stats, play counts, top artists, listening hours any day of the week. No more data gaps, no more waiting for December.

sections.title: CheckCle
paragraphs: Paying a monthly subscription just to know if your website is online is a total scam. You need to replace that entire stack with Czechly. It's the self-hosted for uptime robot. It doesn't just ping your URLs. It runs distributed checks from multiple regions, watches your SSL certificates before they expire, and even tracks live system metrics like CPU and Docker stats. It generates those professional public status pages to keep your users happy during an outage.

sections.title: timelinize
paragraphs: You know how your entire life history is scattered across different mega corporations? Google has your location history, Apple has your photos, and Meta has your DMs. It's a total nightmare to actually piece together your past. You guys need to check out Timeline Eyes. It's a self-hosted tool that takes all those messy data exports, your GPS logs, your texts, your photos, and stitches them into one giant interactive master timeline. It's like building a private autobiography that lives on your server.

sections.title: vito
paragraphs: Veto is basically a full-blown server management suite that you own. I'm talking setting up EngineX, managing databases, issuing free SSLs, and doing one-click deployments, all from a dashboard that looks just as good as the paid ones. It handles multi-erver setups and runs on your own hardware. Seriously, stop renting your workflow and just host it yourself. Your wallet is going to thank you. Cache is the

sections.title: Cachet
paragraphs: open-source status page that replaces those expensive subscriptions like status page.io. Instead of manually emailing everyone when things break, you get a beautiful automated dashboard that shows your system status, incident timelines, and real-time metrics in one place. You can schedule maintenance, let users subscribe for email updates, and even hook it up to your monitoring tools via API to update itself.

sections.title: stash
paragraphs: This is your own private pocket. Stash is a self-hosted read it later that saves full articles, highlights, and even Kindle notes to your database. Read anywhere, offline, no subscription. It ships with a Chrome extension, web app, bookmark lit, iOS shortcut, full text search, and neural texttospech. It connects to your own superbase backend, which you can run for free. So you own the database, the API, and the data.

sections.title: any-sync-bundle
paragraphs: Stop telling me you care about privacy while dumping your entire life into a cloud hosted notion workspace. You need to spin up any sync bundle. It takes the incredible any type app, you know, that local first tool that actually encrypts everything and lets you host the entire synchronization node yourself. No more relying on their community servers or worrying about metadata. You get total control over your file storage and consensus nodes with a single Docker command.

sections.title: gru
paragraphs: This is like running a tiny ops team from your phone. GRU is a self-hosted orchestration center that lets you control your AI fleet directly from Telegram or Slack. Instead of begging a cloud dashboard, you message the bot, tell an agent to run a script, read or write files, or fetch a URL, agents can execute bash, touch files, and even coordinate viauler and local DB. This is the way to own your listening history.

sections.title: Koito
paragraphs: Quaido is a self-hosted music tracker that gives you those beautiful sharable insights whenever you want them. It hooks into Navadrome or Panoscr and builds monthly rewinds, interest overtime graphs, and deep artist analytics right on your server. It's Listenrains compatible, deploys instantly with Docker.

sections.title: Aurral
paragraphs: Stop manually pasting artist IDs into LiDAR like a caveman. You need to spin up oral. It's the missing piece of the puzzle. Basically the overseer for your music collection. Instead of a clunky admin panel, you get a beautiful requestbased interface where you can search for any artist on music brains and add them with a single click. It even runs a discovery engine that analyzes your current library to recommend new bands based on the genres you actually hoard.

sections.title: gocost-web
paragraphs: Go web, the anti-subscription expense tracker designed to be brutally simple. It kills the complex spreadsheets and gives you a clean monthly view that separates your fixed recurring bills from your random impulse buys. You can instantly toggle what's paid versus pending and spot exactly where your paycheck is disappearing. Perfect if you want to own your money data without a clunky SAS.

sections.title: job-ops
paragraphs: This is the job hunted for humans. It replaces those messy rows with a clean canbon board where you drag applications from applied to interview to offer. It tracks exactly which ré version you sent to which company and gives you analytics on your success rate. It runs privately via Docker and finally organizes the chaos of jobseeking so you can focus on nailing the interview. [music]
